page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highmem-1 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the n4a server family. It features a single dedicated ARMv8-based Neoverse-N3 physical core operating at 3.4 GHz, with one thread per core. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 112 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptography, though it lacks AVX, AMX, and SHA_NI instruction sets.

Benchmark data reveals moderate single-core capabilities paired with constrained multi-core and memory performance. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance and Geekbench single-core score both rank in the average tier, and single-threaded gzip compression demonstrates strong performance in the top 25 percent. However, due to the single-core configuration, multi-core CPU benchmarks from stress-ng and Geekbench fall into the poor category. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 71.67 GB/sec and large block uncached read and write speeds registering in the weak bottom 25 percent tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio for lightweight workloads, allowing memory-bound applications to run without paying for unnecessary compute cores. However, the single-core limitation restricts its utility for parallel processing, software compilation, or complex database operations, as reflected in the poor Passmark database and Redis SET performance. It is suited for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic text processing, simple web serving, or small-scale memory-resident applications that do not require high computational throughput.
